symptom: Pairwise blind reviews can attribute a displayed left/right choice to the wrong scheme after random image order; invalid preregistration timestamps block cards; malformed judge JSON is recorded without a bounded retry or blocked count.
direct_cause: The randomized pairwise array labels source identity instead of display position, preregistration accepts model timestamp text before replacing it, and review parsing has no schema-error retry boundary.
class_root: The judge harness lacks one shared boundary that normalizes display positions, owns runner timestamps, and validates every model response with an explicit retry budget.
affected_population: Director review and pairwise JSON responses
internal_only_reason: This is an internal evaluation harness invariant; no third-party behavior decides the display-label, timestamp, or schema-retry contract.
invariants: A model winner is interpreted as a display position first, then mapped to the source scheme occupying that position.
Every persisted preregistration frozenAt is generated by the runner as a valid ISO-8601 instant.
A schema-invalid model response receives at most one schema-error retry and then becomes blocked with a receipt.
A pairwise conclusion is recorded only when forward and reverse display orders agree on the source scheme.

door_reduction.why_not: The runner intentionally keeps separate preregistration, review, pairwise, and report calls so each receipt has an explicit lifecycle; all five doors converge on the judge runner boundaries changed here.

generality_proof: The display-position mapper is used by every pairwise call regardless of card or scheme names; runner-owned timestamp generation covers every preregistration card; the response parser and retry wrapper cover both visual review and pairwise JSON consumers.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Normalize display-position winners to source schemes and enforce the one-retry JSON boundary.
Generate and persist the canonical runner timestamp and hash.
Require forward/reverse pairwise agreement and aggregate retry/blocked receipts.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: All normal and bait visual reviews call the shared review parser.
All pairwise calls call the shared display mapper and parser.
Every selected card uses the runner-owned timestamp path.

recurrence.reason: Any randomized pair, model-generated timestamp, or malformed model response can reproduce the same integrity failure on another card or future run.

prevention.invariant: Display winners are mapped by their actual array position and invalid JSON receives one schema-error retry before blocked.
prevention.failure_mode: An unresolved schema error returns a blocked receipt and is counted in report metadata.
prevention.strategy: Keep model-facing labels positional and normalize all outputs at the shared review boundary before the runner records them.

legacy_paths.rationale: No alternate judge path remains; the existing runner calls are consolidated at the shared boundaries.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls these internal receipt invariants.

migration: Existing reports remain historical receipts; new runs emit canonical timestamps and retry metadata.
residual_risks: Live model calls and image rendering remain external evidence and are not covered by deterministic unit tests.
